newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice prices steady to lower, Malaysia buys.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice prices steady to lower, Malaysia buys.

text.p: Activity in the Thai rice market picked up modestly over the week with Malaysia buying 30,000 tonnes of 100 percent grade B rice, trade sources said on Thursday.
The purchase was made through a recent tender at $330 per tonne FOB Bangkok for prompt delivery, they told Reuters.
"Otherwise there is not much going on in the market, with only small buying here and there," said one trader.

Prices were steady to lower, with the benchmark 100 percent B grade indicated around $340-375 per tonne FOB Bangkok. This was barely changed from last week, although a few traders quoted lower at $330.

The 100 percent fragrant rice was quoted around $680-690 per tonne on the same basis. Prices of other lower grades were mostly easier with the exception of broken rice, which edged up on higher demand.
Market talk that Iran agreed to buy 50,000-60,000 tonnes of Thai rice from private traders for delivery over the next three to four months could not be confirmed.
"There are all sorts of rumours about Iran...Some said they heard it bought from Vietnam. But I guess it has not concluded any deal yet," said a trader from one major exporting firm.
Traders were sceptical about a customs department rice loading report which indicated that four vessels were loading 26,300 tonnes of rice, mostly broken grade, for shipment to India.
"It is very unlikely that India will buy from Thailand. There could be some mistakes in destination declaring," said one Bangkok-based trader.
"But if the report was true, it means India has sold a lot and might have to import from Thailand to cover obligations. That sounds very unlikely, though," he added.
